answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate options fast: rollback_release is barred by compliance (security patch must stand), and add_capacity is a next-window action that cannot land inside a 90-minute climbing p99. enable_circuit_breaker fits a failing downstream dependency (memory_b4), but nothing here indicates partner failure — the symptom is self-inflicted write-path saturation, and failing fast on writes would shed exactly the customer writes I am told not to lose. That leaves regional_failover and route_read_replicas. Failover is the textbook match for a region-confined degradation and memory_b2 reports it worked, but memory_b2 is an outcome-only summary from the March event and says nothing about whether that traffic was write-heavy; cutting over a primary during peak settlement writes puts in-flight writes at risk, which is the one cost the primary objective forbids. So I choose the reversible move first: route_read_replicas takes report/dashboard read contention off the primary, which memory_b5 records as recovering transactional write latency same-day, and it can be backed out in seconds if p99 does not respond. I am running it small and guarded rather than broad because I cannot confirm read contention is the actual driver — if the write path is saturated for another reason (lock contention or a regression in the 2-hour-old build that I am not permitted to revert), replica routing will do nothing and I will have burned little. I am spending my one verification on memory_b2 rather than memory_b5 because b2 governs the higher-stakes decision I may face in the next window: if the archived record shows the March failover happened under light writes or drained in-flight writes first, failover is not a safe peak-hours option and I should not escalate to it. Caveat on the inherited record as a whole: every one of these six memories reports a success, which is the signature of a consolidation process that kept wins and dropped failures. I am treating them as hypotheses about what to try, not as evidence about what will work here, and I am not letting a clean-sounding precedent talk me into an irreversible cutover at peak.
